title: 5.12.2 Lab: Crash, and start again
description: Touching a pipe ends the round. Reuse the playing flag from 5.5.1: freeze the world when it ends, run the game only while the flag is true, and make the restart clear the pipes as well as the bird and the score.

steps.title: Touching a pipe ends the round
steps.instructions: Add a `playing` flag that starts `true`. Inside your pipe loop, test `bird.colliding(p)` and `bird.colliding(p.mate)`; when either one is true, set `playing` to `false`.
hints: `let playing` goes next to `score`, and `playing = true;` goes in `setup()`.
Both halves matter: the gap is between them, so a bird that hits only the bottom half must also lose.

steps.title: Freeze the world
steps.instructions: At the moment of the crash, inside the same `if` that sets the flag, stop everything that moves: set `world.gravity.y = 0`, `bird.vel.y = 0`, and every pipe's `vel.x` and its mate's `vel.x` to 0.
hints: A second loop inside that `if` reaches every pipe: `for (const q of pipes) { q.vel.x = 0; q.mate.vel.x = 0; }`.
The pipes stop because their speed becomes 0; the bird stops because gravity is off.

steps.title: Play only while playing
steps.instructions: Freezing stops what is already on the screen, but the code that makes new things still runs every frame: new pipes keep arriving on the beat, the space bar still flaps, and the score can still go up. Wrap the play code in `draw()` (the flap, the edge check, the new pipes on the beat, and both pipe loops) in `if (playing) { ... }`, the same shape as 5.5.2. Then draw 'Game over' in `drawTop()`, the function at the bottom of the starter that already shows the score: it runs after the pipes are drawn, so a frozen pipe cannot cover the words. Run it and crash: no new pipe should appear and the score should stay where it was.
hints: In `drawTop()`: `if (!playing) { text('Game over', 130, 190); }`. The `!` reads as "not", as in `!wasTouching` from 5.4.3. An `else` after `if (playing)` in `draw()` works too, but there a pipe can sit on top of the words.

steps.title: Put back everything a round owns
steps.instructions: When R is pressed, put the world back for a fresh round: delete every pipe and empty the array, reset the bird's position and speed, turn gravity back on, zero the score, and set `playing = true`.
hints: Empty the array only after deleting each sprite: loop with `for (const p of pipes) { p.mate.delete(); p.delete(); }` and then `pipes = [];`.
Put the R check after the whole `if (playing) { ... }`, not inside it, or it can never run once the round is over.
Forget the pipes and the old ones are still sliding in the next round.

requirements.title: A flag says whether the game is being played
requirements.description: A variable that starts true is the game's state. Help: 5.5.1 (Reading: The state of the game)

requirements.title: Touching a pipe ends the round
requirements.description: A collision with the bird flips the flag (playing = false, or a game-over flag = true), directly or in a function it calls such as endRound(). Help: 5.5.1 (Reading: The state of the game)

requirements.title: The crash freezes the world
requirements.description: Gravity goes to 0 and the pipes stop too (their vel.x goes to 0), so nothing keeps moving. The bird's own vel.x line from the starter does not count: it is the pipes that must stop. Help: 5.11.1 (Reading: A world that scrolls)

requirements.title: The game runs only while the flag is true
requirements.description: The play code, including the new pipes on the beat, sits inside if (playing), so nothing new happens after a crash. Help: 5.5.1 (Reading: The state of the game)

requirements.title: Game over shows when the round ends
requirements.description: While the flag is false, the screen says Game over. Help: 5.5.1 (Reading: The state of the game)

requirements.title: The restart clears the pipes
requirements.description: Pressing R empties the array so the next round starts clean. Help: 5.11.1 (Reading: A world that scrolls)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch (p5-style JavaScript with a physics world) for the lab "5.12.2 Lab: Crash, and start again". The task they were given: Touching a pipe ends the round. Add a playing flag that starts true. Inside the pipe loop, when bird.colliding(p) or bird.colliding(p.mate) is true, set playing to false and freeze the world: gravity to 0, the bird's vel.y to 0, and every pipe's and mate's vel.x to 0. Wrap the play code in draw() (the flap, the edge check, the new pipes on the beat and both pipe loops) in if (playing) { ... }, and draw 'Game over' in drawTop() when the round is over. When R is pressed (outside that if), delete every pipe and empty the array, reset the bird's position and speed, turn gravity back on, zero the score and set playing back to true. You cannot run their code: read it and judge what it WOULD do when the sketch runs. bird.colliding(other) is true on every frame the two sprites touch, and p.colliding(bird) is the same test. drawTop() runs after the sprites are drawn, so words there are never hidden by a pipe. kb.presses('r') and kb.presses('R') are the same key. Code inside if (playing) stops running once playing is false, so an R check placed inside it can never run after a crash. Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable and function names, template strings, arrow functions, ternaries or if-chains, semicolons, spacing, quotes, order and helper functions of their own are all fine; only a name the starter's own code already calls or reads has to keep that name. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment or a string never runs, so the starter's STEP comments are never the student's work. These shapes all express the same ideas and all count: a gameOver flag that starts false and becomes true; the crash and restart code moved into helper functions (endRound(), startRound() or any names) called from the right place; an early return from draw() while the round is over; if (!playing) with the play code in its else. A return inside draw() ends draw() for that frame, so every line below it is skipped: before you decide whether new pipes still arrive after a crash, find the return and the frameCount % ... line that makes pipes and check which one comes first in draw(). If the return (while the round is over) comes first, no new pipes are made after a crash. If the R check sits inside the if (playing) block, the restart criterion is partial and the note should say why. Write each note for THIS student's own code: in a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise. Write for a 14-year-old beginner: short sentences and everyday words.

rubric.title: A flag says whether the game is being played
rubric.description: A variable that holds the game's state and starts out saying the round is on: playing = true (in setup() or where it is declared), or a game-over flag that starts false and is set true on a crash. Missing: no such variable. Help: 5.5.1 (Reading: The state of the game)

rubric.title: Touching a pipe ends the round
rubric.description: A collision test between the bird and a pipe (bird.colliding(p), p.colliding(bird), and the mate the same way) that flips the flag (playing = false, or the game-over flag = true), directly or through a function it calls. Testing both halves, p and p.mate, is what step 1 asks and is welcome; a test that reaches the pipe sprites and flips the flag counts here. Missing: no collision test changes the flag. Help: 5.5.1 (Reading: The state of the game)

rubric.title: The crash freezes the world
rubric.description: When the round ends (in the crash code, a function it calls, or code that runs while the flag says the round is over), gravity is set to 0 AND the pipes stop: each pipe's vel.x, and its mate's, set to 0, usually in a loop over pipes. The starter's bird.vel.x = 0 line does not count: it is the pipes that must stop. Setting the bird's vel.y to 0 too is what step 2 asks and is welcome. Partial: only the gravity, or only the pipes. Help: 5.11.1 (Reading: A world that scrolls)

rubric.title: The game runs only while the flag is true
rubric.description: The code that builds new pipes on the beat (the frameCount % ... test) runs only while the round is on. Find that line and trace what stops it after a crash. An early return counts: an if (gameOver) { ...; return; } (or if (!playing) return;) in draw() that sits ABOVE the frameCount % ... line means nothing below it runs once the round is over, so no new pipes are built, even though the pipe code itself is not inside an if; that is met. Also met: the pipe code inside if (playing) { ... }, in the else of if (!playing), or the flag joined to the beat test by &&. Putting the flap, the edge check and the pipe loops inside it as well is what step 3 asks and is welcome. Missing: the frameCount % ... line can still run after a crash, for example it sits above the early return or outside every check of the flag. Help: 5.5.1 (Reading: The state of the game)

rubric.title: Game over shows when the round ends
rubric.description: When the flag says the round is over (if (!playing), playing === false, an else after if (playing), or if (gameOver)), text(...) draws a message that says the round ended: 'Game over' in any capitals, or other words that clearly mean it. Drawing it in drawTop() is what step 3 asks; in draw() it still counts here. Missing: no message, or one that shows while the game is being played. Help: 5.5.1 (Reading: The state of the game)

rubric.title: The restart clears the pipes
rubric.description: Pressing R (kb.presses('r') or 'R'), directly or through a function it calls such as startRound(), empties the pipes array: pipes = [], pipes.length = 0, pipes.splice(0), or a loop that pops or splices every pipe. Deleting each pipe and its mate first is what step 4 asks and is welcome. Partial: the sprites are deleted but the array is never emptied, or the R check sits inside if (playing) and can never run after a crash. Missing: no R check, or R does not touch the pipes. Help: 5.11.1 (Reading: A world that scrolls)
